concepts.name: Poisson process
concepts.definition: A Poisson process models random events arriving at average rate λ per unit time; inter-arrival times are exponential.

concepts.name: exponential distribution
concepts.definition: The exponential distribution models memoryless waiting times with rate parameter λ.

concepts.name: M/M/1 queue
concepts.definition: An M/M/1 queue has Poisson arrivals, exponential service times, one server, and infinite capacity.

concepts.name: Little's Law
concepts.definition: Little's Law states L = λW: average items in system equals arrival rate times average time in system.

content_chunks.text: Poisson process: events occur independently at rate λ. The number of events in interval t is Poisson(λt). Coin-flip intuition: many rare Bernoulli trials aggregate to Poisson.
Exponential(λ) waiting times are memoryless: P(T > s+t | T > s) = P(T > t). Mean waiting time is 1/λ.
M/M/1 steady-state: utilization ρ = λ/μ must be < 1. Average customers in system L = ρ/(1-ρ).
Little's Law L = λW applies to stable systems and links inventory, throughput, and flow time.
